subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 27, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 27, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS Community,

We're excited to share the latest developments and updates from the AcreetionOS project. As we continue to work towards our goal of creating a user-friendly, privacy-focused Linux distribution based on Arch Linux, we're grateful for the support and contributions from our community.

In recent news, the Shelly 3.1.5 package manager for Arch Linux has been updated to include an Atoll-powered AUR browser, making it easier for users to manage their packages. Additionally, the Shelly 3.1.5 package manager has expanded its support for the AUR, providing users with more options for package management.

We're also pleased to announce that GDB 18.1 has been released, offering improved debugging capabilities for developers. This update is a testament to the hard work and dedication of the AcreetionOS team and our community contributors.

In other news, a prominent Arch Linux developer has resigned after a 10-year run, highlighting the importance of community involvement and the need for fresh perspectives. We're grateful for the contributions of this developer and look forward to continuing to work with the Arch Linux community.

On the development front, we've seen several commits and updates across various repositories. Cobra3282000 has made significant contributions to the project, including a new version of the downgrade-desktop tool that works with crashing screens. We're also excited to see the initial commit of the ember-vulkan repository, which aims to bring Vulkan support to AcreetionOS.

In addition to these updates, we've been working on improving the overall user experience of AcreetionOS. Our goal is to create a distribution that is both user-friendly and secure, and we're committed to achieving this through continuous improvement and community engagement.

We'd like to extend a special thank you to our community contributors, who have been instrumental in shaping the direction of the project. Your contributions, whether through code, feedback, or support, are invaluable to us.

As we move forward, we're excited to continue working with our community to create a Linux distribution that truly reflects the values of freedom, security, and user-friendliness. If you're interested in getting involved, please don't hesitate to reach out to us through our Discord server or GitHub repository.

Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community. We're proud to have you on board and look forward to continuing to work together to create a better Linux distribution for all.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva
Co-Lead Developer, AcreetionOS Project
